skills.name: Expository writing: a profession's advantages and challenges

note.text: Expository writing explains a topic through organised points, reasons and examples. Introduce the profession, then discuss advantages and challenges fairly. Distinguish facts you have checked from personal preferences. Training, working conditions and entry requirements can differ by place and change over time, so do not invent a guaranteed qualification route or income. End by bringing the explanation together rather than adding an unrelated claim.

sections.heading: Understand the ideas
sections.text: Expository writing explains a topic through organised points, reasons and examples. Introduce the profession, then discuss advantages and challenges fairly. Distinguish facts you have checked from personal preferences. Training, working conditions and entry requirements can differ by place and change over time, so do not invent a guaranteed qualification route or income. End by bringing the explanation together rather than adding an unrelated claim.

sections.heading: Apply the ideas locally
sections.text: Original model: Teaching can allow a person to help learners understand new ideas. It also requires preparation, patience and continued learning. A teacher may find progress rewarding, while managing a busy class can be challenging. The training and registration requirements should be checked with an appropriate institution. The profession therefore needs both interest in learners and a realistic understanding of its responsibilities.

sections.heading: Reason and check
sections.text: Make a plan with introduction, advantages, challenges and conclusion. Support each point with an explanation rather than praise or criticism alone. Avoid treating one person's preference as a universal fact. A balanced account can still reach a reasoned personal view.

paper_task.prompt: Choose an imaginary character considering a profession. Explain possible advantages and challenges without inventing current entry requirements or guaranteed earnings.
model: Teaching can allow a person to help learners understand new ideas. It also requires preparation, patience and continued learning. A teacher may find progress rewarding, while managing a busy class can be challenging. The training and registration requirements should be checked with an appropriate institution. The profession therefore needs both interest in learners and a realistic understanding of its responsibilities.
checklist: I introduce and explain the profession.
I support both advantages and challenges.
